question: As of November 2026, which crewed mission holds the record for the farthest distance humans have traveled from Earth?
answer: Artemis II holds that record as of the sources' dates. On 6 April 2026, Orion and its four-person crew flew past the Moon and broke the Apollo 13 record for the farthest distance travelled from Earth [2]. The crew was NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, plus Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen [2]. The sources don't give the exact distance figure for the new record.

studyNotes.focus: The question asks which crewed mission holds the record for the greatest distance humans have traveled from Earth, as of November 2026.

keyPoints.text: Artemis II was the first crewed mission of the Artemis programme, carrying four astronauts around the Moon and back.
On April 6, 2026, Orion and its crew flew past the Moon, breaking the Apollo 13 record for the farthest distance travelled from Earth.
Artemis II splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 11, 2026, after travelling over 1 million km through deep space over about 10 days.
Artemis II is described as the first crewed flight aboard NASA's human deep space capabilities.
Voyager 1 is an uncrewed probe and is not a crewed mission, so it does not count toward the human distance record.

mayBeStale.text: Source 2 is an ESA page dated 2026-10-30 that describes Artemis II as completed; this is current but the Apollo 13 record statement reflects the record at the time of that mission.
Voyager 1 distance and instrument status figures are from late 2026 pages and change over time, though they do not bear on the crewed-record question.
